title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, upgrade actions, and improve cache hygiene
author: Asha Patel
commits: split workflows: move lint, test, and release into separate workflows
upgrade: bump actions/checkout to v4 and setup-node to v4 for Node 20 support
cache hygiene: make cache keys deterministic + prune stale caches
consolidate matrix: align node versions across lint/test jobs
docs: add migration notes and troubleshooting section for cache invalidation
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic ci.yml has grown brittle and long-running; lint/test/release steps are interleaved which slows iteration and makes debugging harder. This PR splits the top-level workflow into three focused workflows (lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml), upgrades several GH Actions to current stable major versions, and improves cache key hygiene to avoid cache pollution across branches and Node versions.

What changed (summary): - New workflows/.github/workflows/lint.yml to run ESLint and license checks; lightweight, runs on PRs. - New workflows/test.yml to run unit + integration tests with a reduced matrix and faster warm startup using more deterministic caching. - New workflows/release.yml to handle tagging, changelog generation, and release automation; requires release label and manual trigger for prod publish. - Upgraded actions/checkout@v3 -> actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v3 -> actions/setup-node@v4; updated uses for cache action and auth scopes. - Cache key improvements: include node-version, package-lock hash, and workflow name; add explicit cache pruning step to avoid stale entries. - Small CI script changes to make npm ci deterministic and to emit metadata for traceability.

Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and validate runs on forked PRs. - [x] Upgrade actions and verify backwards compat. - [x] Validate cache hit/miss behavior across branches. - [x] Update developer docs (CONTRIBUTING.md) with new local workflow commands.

Testing: Ran full matrix on a feature branch and iterated fixes for flaky integration tests. Verified lint.yml exits early on formatting errors and that test.yml's cache key produces repeatable warm starts (cold first build, warm second build). Release workflow tested with manual dry-run using staging tag. CI shows green across all checks after final re-run.
review_comments: Samir Rao: Can we keep the monorepo-level ci.yml as a thin orchestrator that only triggers the smaller workflows? The removed file made it slightly harder to discover the flow.

Asha Patel (author): I considered that; I left an archived ci.yml with a README header that explains the mapping and links to the three workflows. The top-level file was the source of most flakes so removing it improves transparency and reduces duplicated job logic.
Elena Kim: The cache keys look good, but can we include a short TTL policy or pruning on per-branch caches to avoid disk growth on runner hosts?
Asha Patel: Added scripts/ci/cache-prune.sh and a scheduled workflow to run monthly to prune caches older than 60 days; added instructions to runners/ops for manual prune if needed.
Jordan Lee: Release workflow LGTM but please require both release label and manual approval for production publishes. Also add a dry-run mode for staging.
Asha Patel: Added required label gating and manual approval step. Dry-run flag added and was used during testing.
ci_checks: release.yml: manual dry-run passed (no publish in dry-run)
e2e-canary: pending (flaky, gated outside this PR)
release_notes: Refactor CI into separate lint/test/release workflows; upgrade GitHub Actions to v4 where applicable; improve cache key hygiene and add cache pruning; minor CI script fixes and CONTRIBUTING updates for local testing.
notes: This is primarily a repo hygiene and developer experience change. No production runtime changes. Teams should update their local CI/debug commands per CONTRIBUTING.md. Runners operators: consider running cache prune after deployment.
